key_insight: The paper reframes flowchart resizing as a structure-preserving relayout problem: the same ML pipeline figure should remain editable, faithful, and connection-correct across very different aspect ratios. It introduces an agentic pipeline to adapt one figure for many canvases without hallucinating or breaking the graph.
problem_solved: AI/ML figures often need to be reused across paper columns, slides, posters, and mobile/social formats, but naive resizing can distort layout or silently break arrows and connections. This paper tackles the challenge of converting a raster flowchart into a new aspect-ratio-specific layout while preserving the underlying computational structure.
method: Formulates aspect-ratio-adaptive flowchart relayout as a dedicated task.
Takes a raster flowchart plus a target canvas ratio as input.
Uses an agentic pipeline to produce a structurally faithful, editable output instead of a simple resized image.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this makes pipeline figures easier to reuse across publications, presentations, and promotional materials without risking misleading visuals. It can save time in figure adaptation while improving clarity and trustworthiness.
visual_elements: Before-and-after flowchart relayout across multiple aspect ratios
A pipeline diagram showing raster input -> agentic relayout -> editable output
Aspect ratio examples: 1:1, 16:9, 9:16, portrait poster, paper column
Highlighted arrows/connectors showing preserved structure and no broken links
paper_title: One Figure, Every Canvas: Editable Flowchart Relayout via Agentic Pipeline
paper_authors: Shih-Chen Tseng, Chih-Hsuan Chen, Ryan Yang, Hsi-An Chen, Chun-Wei Tuan Mu
